# A ball that contains the intersection of two balls, one-limb center

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone2/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `ball_intersection_1` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

A ball that contains the intersection of two balls, $X$ the ball of center $c_x$ and radius $r_x$ and $Y$ the ball of center $c_y$ and radius $r_y$; the empty set and the whole line included:

$$Z \supseteq X \cap Y.$$

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `X.intersection(Y)` | `Ball<T, 1>`, `Ball<T, 1>` | `Ball<T, 1>` | contains the common members, not claimed the smallest nor inside either; with the whole line as an operand, the other as it is; `constexpr`; rounds, and is preceded by the debug build's check of the rounding mode |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- $X$, of center $c_x$ and radius $r_x$, is a canonical ball: a finite ball (finite center, finite radius $\ge 0$), the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).
- $Y$, of center $c_y$ and radius $r_y$, is a canonical ball: a finite ball (finite center, finite radius $\ge 0$), the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- The result, the ball $Z$ of center $c_z$ and radius $r_z$, is a canonical ball.
- $Z$ contains every real number that is a member of both $X$ and $Y$.
- $Z$ is empty when an operand is; when $X$ is the whole line, $Z$ is $Y$ as it is (the same limbs); when $Y$ is the whole line and $X$ is not, $Z$ is $X$ as it is.
- Not claimed: that $Z$ is inside $X$ or $Y$, nor that it is empty whenever they are disjoint.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `ball_intersection_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeBallHull.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeBallHull.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions ball_intersection_1_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `ball_intersection_1_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** both balls to intervals, their intersection, back to a ball, the empty set selected last (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/ball_intersection_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/ball_intersection_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`sub_down_1`](sub_down_1.md), [`add_up_1`](add_up_1.md), [`interval_to_ball_1`](interval_to_ball_1.md).

```
# A ball with a one-limb center that contains the intersection of two such balls (milestone2.md,
# "One enclosure interface", "Hull, intersection and split of balls"): the values of the composition
# of ball_to_interval_1 of each ball, interval_intersection_1 and interval_to_ball_1. If X is the whole
# line Y is returned as it is, and if Y is the whole line and X is not, X (the same limbs), by the
# tests of the radii; two whole lines give Y, whose center may be -0 where X's is +0, which is why
# the second clause has its condition. An empty operand gives the empty set, and so do two balls
# whose intervals do not meet. The listing computes those values in
# another order: the directed bounds of both balls and their intersection [l, h] as they are, the
# ball of interval_to_ball_1 of [l, h], and only then the empty set selected, when a radius is a NaN
# (an empty ball, which ball_to_interval_1 makes the empty interval) or l > h (which
# interval_intersection_1 makes the empty interval, and interval_to_ball_1 the empty ball, a NaN
# center and radius). Where the conversions select the constants of the empty interval before the
# halving of interval_mid_rad_1, GCC 13 on x86-64 duplicates the halving, its two products included,
# on the path where the bounds are those constants (4 fused multiply-adds for 2, which the
# object-code check refuses); selected after it, the products are computed once. The selects choose
# the composition when neither operand is the whole line (nx, ny) and the intersection is not empty
# (ob), the case the scalar printer puts first. Not claimed: that the result is inside X or Y (the
# two outward conversions can make it stick out by a rounding), nor that it is empty whenever the
# balls are disjoint.

xl     = sub_down_1(cx, rx)
xu     = add_up_1(cx, rx)
yl     = sub_down_1(cy, ry)
yu     = add_up_1(cy, ry)
ml     = lt(xl, yl)
l      = select(ml, yl, xl)
mu     = lt(yu, xu)
h      = select(mu, yu, xu)
(c, r) = interval_to_ball_1(l, h)
ok     = le(l, h)
qx     = eq(rx, rx)
qy     = eq(ry, ry)
oa     = and(ok, qx)
ob     = and(oa, qy)
cb     = select(ob, c, const nan)
rb     = select(ob, r, const nan)
wx     = eq(rx, const inf)
nx     = not(wx)
wy     = eq(ry, const inf)
ny     = not(wy)
ca     = select(ny, cb, cx)
ra     = select(ny, rb, rx)
cz     = select(nx, ca, cy)
rz     = select(nx, ra, ry)
```

## Measured

The latest brute-force runs, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#ball_intersection_1)): the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound.
They judged the kernel in the extended domain, infinite and NaN operands included, as the oracle reads its statement in the IEEE model ([Claims of the non-finite layer](../developer/architecture.md#claims-of-the-non-finite-layer)).

| Run | Cases judged | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 7 200 000 | 0 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 7 200 000 | 0 |
| toy formats, every operand: 3 domains of 3 formats | 3 420 868 | 0 |

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
